scope: Independent read-only visual comparison of four candidate masks against four named community icon captures; not publisher/canonical certification

macroFindings: The large inset oval/circular forehead field, image-left damaged/starburst mark and slanting claw-like cheek scoring are preserved.
The rounded lower face, narrow eye region and visible asymmetry remain coherent with the icon.
No long white dreads have been converted into mask points.
The broad engraved forehead, two upper light slots, large oval eye/goggle regions, central bridge and bilateral cheek vent panels are preserved.
No new crown horns or long hair are present.
The identity remains distinct from a generic Jungle-style plate.
uncertainDetails: The exact ownership/extent of the long pale side pieces is difficult to separate from the generic pale port head at256px; do not certify these as original PHG side geometry without a clearer model view.

macroFindings: The split upper crown, central round/oval inset, paired pointed inner rim and decorated upper lateral lobes are preserved.
The dark forehead mark, narrowing brow, pointed cheek panels and central ridged lower shape remain coherent with the source.
Generic long white dreads are omitted.
uncertainDetails: Small temple perforations and upper decorative line counts cannot be established exactly from the source resolution.

macroFindings: The layered upper crest, broad divided forehead panel, central vertical lower strip and two sweeping cheek bands are preserved.
The image-native near-front view and lower pointed outline remain coherent with the icon; no new fangs/dreads are present.
uncertainDetails: Exact groove depth, slot count on the small central strip and small surface scars remain unqualified.

conclusion: No sufficiently certain major silhouette, crown-count or asymmetry mismatch was found that warrants an unconditional new generation. Minor lines, ports, pale head/side-piece boundaries and materials remain source-limited and must not be advertised as original PHG1:1.
